items.note: The verify template has no labels for these three checks, so no field or literal kind can confirm the 'not verified' marking when the spec is absent or empty.

sources.quote: If those spec files are absent or empty, mark **Spec Coverage**, **Requirement Implementation Mapping**, and **Scenario Coverage** as not verified

items.note: Needs a semantic judgement on whether an unlabeled check is reported as clean when the spec is missing; no kind can express this.

sources.quote: do not treat any of them as clean.

items.note: No kind connects search commands to the keywords of each requirement.

sources.quote: For each ADDED or MODIFIED requirement ... Search codebase for keywords related to the requirement

items.note: The condition (a requirement looks unimplemented) is a semantic judgement, and no predicate can express it.

sources.quote: If ADDED or MODIFIED requirements appear unimplemented: - Add CRITICAL issue: "Requirement not found: <requirement name>"

items.note: This applies only when a requirement is unimplemented, which is a semantic condition that cannot be expressed.
Requires the REMOVED requirement names from the delta spec. The heading text 'REMOVED Requirements' does not appear literally in the cited lines, so a scoped cross_ref cannot be built.

sources.quote: Never report a REMOVED requirement as "Requirement not found" or recommend implementing it.

items.note: The condition (the removed behavior is still in the code) is a semantic judgement.

sources.quote: If the behavior is still present: - Add CRITICAL issue: "Removed requirement still implemented: <requirement name>"

items.note: This applies only when the removed behavior is still present, which is a semantic condition.

sources.quote: Recommendation: "Remove the remaining implementation at <file>:<lines>, following the requirement's Migration note if it has one"

items.note: The format of the FROM entries in the RENAMED section is not fixed, so the names cannot be extracted reliably for a disjointness check.

sources.quote: Do not report the FROM name as missing

items.note: The main spec is not a SOURCE id usable by doc_read, and the condition (a RENAMED entry exists that is not also MODIFIED) cannot be expressed.

sources.quote: Otherwise, read the baseline requirement in the main spec at `<planningHome.root>/openspec/specs/<capability-path>/spec.md`, using the same capability path as the delta spec

items.note: The condition (the renamed behavior looks unimplemented) is a semantic judgement.

sources.quote: If it appears unimplemented: - Add CRITICAL issue: "Renamed requirement not found: <TO name>"

items.note: This applies only when the renamed behavior is unimplemented, which is a semantic condition.

sources.quote: Recommendation: "Restore the behavior of <TO name> (renamed from <FROM name>); a rename must not change behavior"

items.note: The condition (the baseline cannot be found or read for a RENAMED entry) cannot be expressed, and the verify template has no Spec Coverage label.

sources.quote: If the baseline requirement cannot be found or read, mark **Spec Coverage** as not verified for that entry with the reason.

items.note: No predicate can express the condition 'removal or rename only' over the delta spec sections, and there are no template labels for these checks.

sources.quote: If the delta specs are readable and contain at least one REMOVED or RENAMED requirement but no ADDED or MODIFIED requirements

items.note: Same unexpressible removal/rename-only condition as vf-088.

sources.quote: so do not mark these two checks as not verified.

items.note: The condition (no parseable requirements in the delta) and the target checks (no template labels) cannot be expressed.

sources.quote: A delta spec with no parseable requirements at all is unusable evidence, not a removal-only change: mark these checks as not verified.
